_doc: tools/raw_depth_check.py's classification of every non-tail recursion in the raw host code (host/native/*.lisp), with tools/depth_check.py's rules: bounded names its bound (a *constant* the tree defines, a number, or a structural bound); debt only shrinks; operator data is never a bound (D27).  Introduced empty of debt (lane depth-debt, 2026-09-28).

bounded.fnn-clone-copy-tree: the checkpoint clone's directory depth: it refuses past max-depth, fn-cpa-clone-max-depth = *fn-cpa-clone-max-depth* (books/checkpoint-auxiliary.lisp)
bounded.fnn-dispatch: recurses once, for a bare `fn', with the fixed argv (operator - help), which is not empty: depth 2
bounded.fnn-export-sync-tree: the export archive's directory layout: fn-sxd-program (books/store-export-durability.lisp) makes only config/ and records/ under the archive, so the depth is 2
bounded.fnn-guard-conjuncts: the if-nesting height of an entry's translated guard, a term the image's own source declares (fixed at build), not data
bounded.fnn-mux-begin-drain: the mux connection state machine: fnn-mux-after never re-enters fnn-mux-work for the connection whose work loop is running (the working-connection mark it binds), and a TLS handshake started inside a call cannot finish inside it (SSL_accept needs the peer's Finished, a round trip): a fixed nesting, not per command or connection
bounded.fnn-mux-flush: the mux connection state machine: fnn-mux-after never re-enters fnn-mux-work for the connection whose work loop is running (the working-connection mark it binds), and a TLS handshake started inside a call cannot finish inside it (SSL_accept needs the peer's Finished, a round trip): a fixed nesting, not per command or connection
bounded.fnn-mux-handshake-step: the mux connection state machine: fnn-mux-after never re-enters fnn-mux-work for the connection whose work loop is running (the working-connection mark it binds), and a TLS handshake started inside a call cannot finish inside it (SSL_accept needs the peer's Finished, a round trip): a fixed nesting, not per command or connection
bounded.fnn-mux-install-compress: the same fixed nesting: its non-tail call is fnn-mux-z-in, whose own bound is the terminal fnn-mux-finish; the compression layer is installed once per connection (the 206 is answered once, ACL2 decides fn-auth-compress), and the stash it serves is one served read: fnn-mux-after never re-enters fnn-mux-work for the connection whose work loop is running (the working-connection mark it binds), and a TLS handshake started inside a call cannot finish inside it (SSL_accept needs the peer's Finished, a round trip): a fixed nesting, not per command or connection
bounded.fnn-mux-request-handshake: the same fixed nesting: its non-tail calls are fnn-mux-start-handshake, whose first fnn-mux-handshake-step cannot complete SSL_accept (it returns :input or :output), and fnn-mux-handshake-refused, whose only call is the terminal fnn-mux-finish: fnn-mux-after never re-enters fnn-mux-work for the connection whose work loop is running (the working-connection mark it binds), and a TLS handshake started inside a call cannot finish inside it (SSL_accept needs the peer's Finished, a round trip): a fixed nesting, not per command or connection
bounded.fnn-mux-start-waiting-handshake: the mux connection state machine: fnn-mux-after never re-enters fnn-mux-work for the connection whose work loop is running (the working-connection mark it binds), and a TLS handshake started inside a call cannot finish inside it (SSL_accept needs the peer's Finished, a round trip): a fixed nesting, not per command or connection
bounded.fnn-mux-work: the mux connection state machine: fnn-mux-after never re-enters fnn-mux-work for the connection whose work loop is running (the working-connection mark it binds), and a TLS handshake started inside a call cannot finish inside it (SSL_accept needs the peer's Finished, a round trip): a fixed nesting, not per command or connection
bounded.fnn-mux-z-in: the same fixed nesting: its non-tail call is the terminal fnn-mux-finish, which at most starts the waiting handshakes (a loop over the queue, each started handshake returning before it can complete): fnn-mux-after never re-enters fnn-mux-work for the connection whose work loop is running (the working-connection mark it binds), and a TLS handshake started inside a call cannot finish inside it (SSL_accept needs the peer's Finished, a round trip): a fixed nesting, not per command or connection
bounded.fnn-owner-feed-v1-peers: the FNFD v1 namespace's directory depth: it faults past (fnn-feed-filename-max-v1-chunks) = *fn-ff-max-v1-chunks* (books/feed-filename.lisp)
bounded.fnn-tcl-apply: depth 2: its non-tail call (through fnn-tcl-turn-lost, which applies the tcp-closed result) is under the :refused arm of the passive admission, which runs once per connection because fnn-tclc-session-admitted is set before the admission is asked, so the inner apply skips it
